body.x: [Las Vegas, U.S. = Aving News] DeepBrain AI Inc. (CEO Eric Jang) announced that they participated in CES 2023 held in Las Vegas, U.S. for four days from Thursday, January 5 to Sunday, January 8, 2023 in local time.
DeepBrain AI is a provider of artificial intelligence (AI) avatar generation solutions supported by thousands of scenarios.

Their solution is largely divided into three types: △AI Human (a real-time interactive digital human development, testing, and creation solution utilized in web and mobile environments), △AI Studios (a script and video SaaS platform that can create, edit, and synthesize digital content with digital human in minutes), △AI Kiosk (a solution that provides digital human engagement on edge and cloud using NLP and interactive windows).

With these services, users can create avatars by using real-time video synthesis technology, and their requests get immediate responses with required information, guidance, and troubleshooting for better user experience and satisfaction.

The services’ technical characteristics can be further employed to interact in person in real time, and to model an actual person’s appearance, gestures, and even local dialect, offering advantages that other solutions can't provide. In fact, the Republic of Korea's President Seok-Yeol Yoon, Korean national soccer player Heung-Min Son, and America’s Got Talent’s judge Howie Mandel were embodied as avatars.

body.cap: DeepBrain AI's AI avatar solution AI Kiosk | Photo by Aving News

body.x: Moreover, DeepBrain AI's solution can create its own AI avatars, but users can choose an option for ready-made products as well. There are also more than 60 AI avatar models available for multilingual conversation and recognition covering English, Korean, and Chinese for high versatility in different situations and countries. The business offers modeling that can best represent a particular service or brand with an excellent avatar implementation and specificity, which is expected to be quite useful in the advertising market.

According to a DeepBrain AI representative, “Under the current trend that necessitates rapid information distribution, we are here to promote our proprietary solutions to the global marketplace.” They added “We will meet with enterprise innovation experts and decision makers who want to digitize, enhance, and differentiate specific services to discuss collaboration and sales.”

In regard to a new service that is currently under development, the representative explained that, “We are working on a service that enables people who lost their loved one to meet and talk with those who passed away using AI technology.” “Our emphasis is on overcoming the limitations of existing unilateral messages such as recordings and videos, and implementing a true two-way communication. It will be established as a means of bonding with the deceased and a new form of remembrance.”

Meanwhile, DeepBrain AI service is powered by big data and artificial intelligence (AI) technology. AI learning requires a large amount of various data to be accumulated. In addition to the data collected on its own, DeepBrain AI was able to enhance the performance of their existing AI models by utilizing publicly accessible AI learning data through AI-Hub established by the Ministry of Science and ICT and the National Information Society Agency.

Organized by the Ministry of Science and ICT and promoted by the National Information Society Agency, the data building project for AI learning which has built a total of 1,300 types of data, will remain open to the public via AI-Hub until 2025. This project has addressed the difficulty in data building, which typically has high costs in terms of time and money, driving the growth of AI SMEs and startups in Korea. AI learning data can be accessed and downloaded by the public on the AI-Hub website.
